title: TypeScript: classes
summary: Write a class with typed properties, a constructor and a method, since every Angular component is a class.

quiz.q: Which keyword creates an object from a class?
quiz.explain: `new Student('Asha', 72)` runs the constructor and returns a fresh object.

quiz.q: Fill in the keyword that hides a property from code outside the class.
quiz.explain: `private` allows access only inside the class. `public` (the default) allows access everywhere.
`public size` in the constructor creates a property `size` set to 4. `double()` returns 4 * 2.

quiz.q: What does `class Student implements Person` promise?
options: Student inherits all code from Person
Student has at least the properties and methods Person describes
quiz.explain: `implements` checks that the class matches the interface. Unlike `extends`, it copies no code.

exercise.task:
Complete the `Student` class in `student.ts`.

- The class `implements Person`.
- The constructor takes `public name: string` and `private marks: number`.
- Add a method `isPassed()` that returns a `boolean`: true when `this.marks >= 40`.
- At the bottom create `const asha = new Student('Asha', 72);`.
hints: Put the class keyword line first: `export class Student implements Person {`.
A constructor parameter with `public` or `private` in front becomes a property automatically.

checks.name: The constructor has a public name: string
The constructor has a private marks: number
checks.hint: Use private marks: number as the second parameter.

checks.name: An object asha is created with new Student('Asha', 72)
